findings.description: This test deliberately runs `tool.main()` on the claude-headless transport WITHOUT the `fake` fixture, with a 400K-token upper bound and a $20 budget, and relies on an ambient CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN sentinel (asserted separately by test_p11_the_module_default_binary_is_a_sentinel_that_does_not_exist) to make the spawn fail. The test receives `monkeypatch` but only uses it for argv; it never pins CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN itself. The reviewer context shows the suites were run under `env -u CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN`, which indicates the module-level sentinel does not override an inherited value. An operator who uses the CLI route legitimately exports CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN to the real binary; in that shell the sentinel test fails loudly but this test still executes and reaches a real `claude -p`.
findings.failure_mode: On a developer or CI host with CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN exported to a real claude binary (and Bedrock/Anthropic credentials present), the unit test sends real 400K-token prompts and bisects downward until the $20 budget or a result is reached: real spend and real provider calls from `pytest`, exactly the zero-spend guarantee the P11 fix claims to make fail-closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Inside the test, set `monkeypatch.setenv("CLAUDE_HEADLESS_BIN", str(tmp_path / "loa-probe-no-real-cli"))` (and `monkeypatch.delenv` any AWS/Anthropic credential vars) before calling `main()`, so the fail-on-spawn property does not depend on import-time state or the invoking shell. Consider also making the module-level sentinel an unconditional assignment rather than setdefault, or an autouse fixture that forces it unless the `fake` fixture is active.

findings.cross_file_justification: test_p7_stdin_is_delivered_and_the_child_leads_its_own_group pins that `_run_capped` places the child in its own process group (and, if implemented via start_new_session, its own session). test_an_interrupt_after_paid_steps_still_writes_the_record is the only KeyboardInterrupt coverage, and it monkeypatches `_run_capped` away entirely, so the interrupt never occurs while a real child is running. The combination leaves the interrupt-during-communicate path of `_run_capped` in tools/ceiling-probe-live.py unexercised.
findings.description: Once the child leads its own group/session, a terminal Ctrl-C delivers SIGINT only to the Python parent, not to `claude -p`. If `_run_capped` kills the group only on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` (the case the P7 test exercises) and not on KeyboardInterrupt/BaseException, the operator's interrupt raises inside `communicate()`, main() writes the record and exits 130, and the orphaned CLI child continues to completion in its own session. The diff's tests cannot detect this because the interrupt test replaces `_run_capped` before any child exists.
findings.failure_mode: Operator presses ^C mid-attempt: the probe exits 130 with `stop: interrupted`, but the real `claude -p` request still completes against the provider, billing the full attempt, and the process lingers as an orphan until the API call returns. The record's `interrupted_estimate` charge happens to cover the cost, but the child is not stopped and any subsequent re-run overlaps with it (ITPM contention, the exact 429 class the TPM backoff logic then has to absorb).
findings.suggested_fix: In `_run_capped`, wrap the `communicate()` call in `try/finally` (or `except BaseException: os.killpg(pgid, SIGKILL); raise`) so the group is killed on any exit path, not just TimeoutExpired. Add a test alongside the P7 pair that spawns the GRANDCHILD wrapper via the real `_run_capped`, sends SIGINT to the test process (or raises KeyboardInterrupt via a timer/signal handler) during the wait, and asserts the grandchild is dead.

findings.description: The pidfile wait loop runs only after `_run_capped` has already raised TimeoutExpired, i.e. after the wrapper has been killed; the pidfile can no longer appear at that point, so the 10-second poll is dead time. If the 2-second cap fires before the wrapper has executed `open(...).write(...)` (slow interpreter start on a loaded runner), the test burns the 10 s deadline and then crashes with FileNotFoundError at `int(pidfile.read_text())` instead of a readable assertion. In that same scenario the grandchild may already have been spawned by Popen but its pid is unknown, so the cleanup `os.kill(gc, 9)` never runs and a 300-second sleeper leaks if the group kill under test is in fact broken.
findings.failure_mode: Flaky, hard-to-diagnose failure on slow CI (FileNotFoundError with no indication that the timeout simply pre-empted the pidfile write), plus a possible orphaned sleeper for 5 minutes when the kill path regresses.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the wrapper write the pidfile before anything slow (or have the test poll for the pidfile in a thread started before `_run_capped`, with a timeout longer than the 2 s cap); replace the bare `read_text()` with `assert pidfile.exists(), "wrapper never reached the pidfile write within the cap"`; and increase the cap to something comfortably above interpreter start (e.g. 5 s) so the test measures group-kill behaviour rather than spawn latency.
